biomarkers.name: MSI / dMMR
biomarkers.prevalence: ~5-35% overall (higher in duodenal tumors and Lynch-associated disease; generally enriched vs CRC)
biomarkers.clinical_use: IO benefit — pembrolizumab; Lynch workup essential

biomarkers.name: KRAS, NRAS, BRAF
biomarkers.prevalence: KRAS ~40-55%; NRAS uncommon; BRAF V600E uncommon (generally <10%)
biomarkers.clinical_use: RAS/RAF profiling is commonly performed, but anti-EGFR benefit in small bowel adenocarcinoma is not established as in CRC; BRAF V600E may support targeted therapy in selected cases

biomarkers.name: CDX2, CK20
biomarkers.clinical_use: Supports GI/intestinal origin in metastatic setting

histomorphological_subtype.primary_pattern: Adenocarcinoma similar to colorectal — tubular / glandular architecture; duodenum most common location
variants: ampullary — treated separately as ampullary carcinoma

tumor_microenvironment.immune_context: Higher MSI-H/dMMR rate than CRC in some subsets → more inflamed subset
tumor_microenvironment.stromal_features: Desmoplastic, similar to other GI adenocarcinomas

cellular_states_and_lineage.cell_of_origin: Small bowel enterocytes / intestinal stem cells at crypt base
cellular_states_and_lineage.developmental_lineage: Endoderm — duodenum from foregut/midgut; jejunum and ileum from midgut
cellular_states_and_lineage.differentiation_state: Intestinal-type glandular differentiation (often CDX2+/CK20+, sometimes MUC2+); resembles colorectal adenocarcinoma but with a distinct molecular profile
cellular_states_and_lineage.lineage_plasticity: Can arise through an adenoma-carcinoma sequence, particularly in familial syndromes such as FAP, but with distinct molecular features and lower APC alteration frequency than CRC
